4	what Prelude ships (`server/views/layout.eta`, the `.bar`/`.page`/`.workspace`

6	Prelude Design System. Gallery: `/gallery` (with `/drawer`, `/modal`,

8	
9	## Layouts
10	
11	- **app** - the bar, then the page scrolling with the window. Pages hold their
12	  own width (`.center`); the shell gives the room above and below. Projects, a
13	  project, Build.
14	- **workspace** - the bar, then the page filling the rest of the window; the
15	  window doesn't scroll, the page's panels do. A design's page (chat + surface).

The design is empty so far, so I read the app's current home page (`server/views/_home.eta`) and the project page (`_folder.eta`). Today the home page knows only each project's name and path. Each project's own page already shows what's in progress there: designs on branches, stories still to build, branches waiting to be finished.

**My proposal:** make the home page answer **"what needs me, and where was I?"** across every recent project.

1. **Needs you** (at the top): one row per item waiting on the person, from any project. Each row names the project, the design and what's needed, and links straight there. Items would include:
   - a design whose screens are ready to build
   - a branch that's been pushed and is waiting on its pull request
   - a build that stopped
   - maybe an agent turn that finished while they were away, or one waiting on an approval
2. **Projects**: the recent projects as a list, each with its path, how many designs are in progress, the app's stack and when it last changed. It would be sorted by most recent.
3. **Open a project**: shrinks to a button and a compact form in the page header. When someone has no projects yet it stays the whole page, which is today's screen.

What the agent is working on right now stays in the bar, which the shell already shows. The page wouldn't repeat it.

**Questions before I build it:**
- **Across projects, or not?** The alternative is to keep home as a simple picker and leave the work view to each project's page. I recommend across projects, because "Needs you" is the main reason to have a dashboard.
- **Turns and approvals:** should "Needs you" include finished agent turns and approvals? The shell has the same open question for its agent status, so we could settle both at once.
- **How many projects** does someone usually have? A handful suits cards; many suits a dense list.
- **Cost:** a dashboard means the server reads every recent project's branches each time the page loads. Is that acceptable, or should it load in the background after the page appears?

I've written this proposal and the questions into `prelude/landing-page/NOTES.md`. Once you've answered, I'll build it with realistic states: typical, first run with no projects, and nothing waiting on you.

I've built the first version of the dashboard. I haven't rendered it yet, so please check it in the preview.

**Home (`/`)**
- **Needs you** (at the top): one row per thing waiting on you, from every project, newest first. Each row has the design, a label for what kind of thing it is, one sentence saying what's needed, and the project and when it happened. The labels are "Asking you", "Build stopped", "Turn finished", "Ready to build" and "Pull request open". A row takes you to where you'd deal with it. A pull request opens on your Git server instead.
- **Projects**: one card per project, most recently changed first. Each card shows its designs in progress as links, a "2 waiting on you" label when something there needs you, and a line with how many designs it has, its app stack and when it last changed. "Open a project…" sits beside the heading and opens the form in a modal.

**Loading states**
- The page appears straight away with each project's name and folder, since the list of recent projects is cheap to read.
- "Needs you" and the contents of the projects then load separately, each in its own part of the page. Until they arrive, grey placeholder bars stand where the content will go, and they pulse gently.
- If one part can't be loaded, it says so and offers **Try again**. The rest of the page still works.
- To look at the loading state on its own, open **"Home, while it loads"** (`/loading`). That page exists only so the preview can show the loading state; the app doesn't need it.

**States:** typical, first run (no projects, so the page is just "Open your first project"), all caught up (nothing needs you), and long names.

**Design system:** it had no placeholder bars, so I added a general `.skeleton` component with its own file, an entry in the components gallery and a line in its NOTES.md. The shell's gallery still draws its own placeholders and could switch to this one.

`RULES.md` has six proposed rules covering what the screens can't show. For example, a finished turn leaves "Needs you" once you open its session, and a pull request stays until it's merged.

**Open questions** (also in NOTES.md):
- Should the parts of the page refresh on their own while the page is open?
- If a project's folder has disappeared, should its card say so and let you remove it?
- Should the "Needs you" count also show in the bar?

**Finished turns expiring:** done. A finished turn now leaves "Needs you" after a week if you never open its session. I picked a week as a first guess, so change it if you like. The other kinds don't expire, because they stay true until something changes them: a question still needs an answer, and a stopped build is still stopped. I've updated rule R-8hc and NOTES.md.

**Connections and events instead of polling:** I think it's a good idea, as long as the page holds one connection rather than one per part of it.

- **Polling is the expensive way here.** Each refresh means reading every project's branches, every 30 seconds, even when nothing has changed.
- **Prelude itself causes almost every change.** It runs the agent's turns, approvals, builds and pushes, so it knows the moment one of them changes something.
- **The plumbing already exists.** The app streams to session pages over server-sent events (`server/live.js`), and Koda reconnects a dropped connection by itself.

The shape I'd use:
1. **One channel per page, opened by the shell's layout**, so every page has it, including the "Needs you" count in the bar.
2. **The server sends small named events** such as `needs-changed`, and each part of the page reloads itself when one arrives. Neither the server nor the page needs any custom code for this.
3. **Keep a slow poll, every few minutes, as a backstop** for what Prelude can't see happen, mainly a pull request merged on the Git server.

One limit: the preview has no channel to receive events from, so in this design the refresh would still be the 30-second poll. The events would only start working once the app is built.

Shall I make that change? It touches the shell's layout as well as this design. I've noted it as an open question in NOTES.md for now.
